$comment: Accepted exceptions for the map-audit skill (.claude/skills/map-audit). A decision with verdict 'accepted' suppresses matching findings on every future run, so a deliberate choice never gets re-litigated. Written ONLY on an explicit human call — never by an agent acting on its own judgement.

$schema_notes.rule: the rule code being excepted, e.g. 'SCAV-1'. See rules.md.
$schema_notes.scope: which tiles the exception covers. Every key present must match. An empty scope {} excepts the whole rule world-wide — use sparingly. Keys: zone_id, terrain, region_id, district, name, map_id (each accepts a string or an array), and name_pattern (a case-insensitive regex).
$schema_notes.verdict: 'accepted' suppresses the finding. 'todo' records the decision without suppressing, for things deferred rather than accepted.
$schema_notes.decided_by: who made the call — a real person. 'John' or 'Dave'.
$schema_notes.reason: why. Written for the person who finds this in a year and wonders.

decisions.reason: Genuinely always-open thresholds, reviewed building by building. Architect Shrine opens on a nave and is open to the faithful; The Ascension Gate's interior IS the checkpoint (The Scanline), so a door in front of it would be a redundant second threshold; KSAB Audience Gate is the public audience entrance to a broadcast lobby. The other 38 doorless buildings all got doors in the same pass.

The Echelon is the one legitimately dynamic entrance in the world: plugins/yacht/index.js sets flags.entrance from whichever pier she ties up against and deletes it while she is underway. A hardcoded cardinal interior link would contradict her the moment she docks on a different side, so 'in' is correct here and must stay.

flags.terrain is the GROUND-surface SSOT and the Echelon is a vessel, not ground — her exterior tile sails, so any painted terrain would be wrong somewhere on the route. Every other outdoor tile on the map was painted in the same pass; this is the single deliberate omission.

Her four neighbours are open Coldwater Basin water. You do not step off the bay onto a moving yacht — boarding goes through the gangway, which the yacht plugin gates on the invite list. Linking these would be a way aboard that bypasses that check.

Open bay — Coldwater Basin, The Meltwater, The Meltwater Mouth. You do not `search` open water, you fish it, and the fishing plugin already models this deliberately: fishingTableFor() returns null ON a water tile because you cast FROM the bank, and water-ADJACENT tiles get fish_coldwater_bay for free. A scavenging table here would duplicate a system that already covers the case correctly. Surface bay only — the sub-surface tiles carry no region_id and are logged separately as todo.

Sub-surface water at z-1 and z-2. Unlike the open bay these are divable and wreck-salvage loot down here would be real content — but underwater scavenging does not exist yet, so this is deferred, not declined. Left as todo so it keeps counting and does not quietly become a 'never'. Revisit with the diving content in docs/systems-swimming.md.

The deep wastes stay empty on purpose. The wilderness is meant to be hostile and unrewarding — loot lives in the city and in the hot zones, and the 960 tiles at radiation >= 38 already carry scav_irradiated_salvage. Giving the other 2,071 a general table would make search-anywhere the default and dilute what makes the irradiated band worth crossing.

The Reach is unbuilt, not broken: 396 of its 400 tiles have no name and no description (they are still 'The Reach 863,1948' / 'An empty place.'). Loot tables before prose is backwards, so this waits on the region being authored. Deliberately todo rather than accepted — it should keep showing up until The Reach is actually built.
